blocks.x: Applying IoT, Twin & Robotics to Automotive & Discrete Manufacturing: the context that decides the design, the weekly cadence, the towers involved, and committed outcomes per gate.

Automotive and discrete plants chase three numbers — OEE, escapes and launch time. Sensor network, vision inspection and scheduling intelligence move all three simultaneously, while IATF traceability and IT/OT security raise the baseline every program must respect.

items: Legacy lines uninstrumented; OEE components and energy per unit are estimates.
Defect detection by eyes/sampling; escapes reach customers and recalls cost millions.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Connected Products & Smart Devices, Smart Infrastructure, Buildings & Cities, Connected Products & Smart Devices from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Line changeover sequencing, Vision inspection, Predictive maintenance) on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — IATF 16949 among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.
Cameras into instruments: inspection, safety and counting at the edge, inside policy.
Fix it before it fails: RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders.
Retrofit sensing on live lines with governed telemetry (OEE components real)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: Ex-rated/industrial sensing on live lines with governed telemetry (critical assets instrumented without stoppage). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
